from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Intuition of Limits: The Squirrel's Path", [
            "The squirrel approaches the tree hollow at x=1.",
            "The path y=(x²-1)/(x-1) shows a missing point.",
            "Height 2 is the destination, the limit L."
        ])
        
        # Axes for the graph
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.add(axes)
        
        # Curve y = (x^2-1)/(x-1) = x+1 for x != 1
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: x + 1, x_range=[0, 2.5], color=WHITE)
        self.add(curve)
        
        # Squirrel asset
        squirrel = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/squirrel.svg", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(squirrel, 'E2', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        # Tree asset
        tree = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tree.svg", color="#32CD32")
        self.place_at_grid(tree, 'B3', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Hollow at (1, 2)
        hollow = Circle(radius=0.08, color="#FF4500", fill_opacity=0).move_to(axes.c2p(1, 2))
        self.add(hollow)
        
        missing_point_label = Text("Hole", font_size=20, color="#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(missing_point_label, 'D3', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.play(FadeIn(squirrel))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")
        self.play(FadeIn(missing_point_label), Create(hollow))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#32CD32")
        self.play(FadeIn(tree))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Limit Toolkit", [
            "Limits bridge static algebra and dynamic calculus.",
            "Epsilon-Delta proofs ensure logical rigor.",
            "L'Hôpital's Rule offers efficient computation."
        ])
        
        # Create icons using assets
        squirrel = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/squirrel.svg").set_color("#FFD700")
        drone = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/drone.svg").set_color("#00BFFF")
        # Slope ratio icon for L'Hopital
        slope_line = Line(LEFT*0.5, RIGHT*0.5, color="#FF6347")
        slope_ratio = VGroup(
            Tex("f'(x)", font_size=24, color="#FF6347"),
            slope_line,
            Tex("g'(x)", font_size=24, color="#FF6347")
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        
        # Groups for easier placement
        sq_group = VGroup(squirrel, Text("Intuition", font_size=18)).arrange(DOWN)
        ed_group = VGroup(drone, Text("Rigor", font_size=18)).arrange(DOWN)
        lh_group = VGroup(slope_ratio, Text("Shortcut", font_size=18)).arrange(DOWN)
        
        toolkit_box = RoundedRectangle(height=1.0, width=3.0, corner_radius=0.2, color=WHITE)
        toolkit_label = Text("Limit Toolkit", font_size=24).move_to(toolkit_box.get_center())
        toolkit_group = VGroup(toolkit_box, toolkit_label)

        # Place grid elements on the right (Columns 4-6 as per requirement)
        self.place_at_grid(sq_group, 'C4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(ed_group, 'C5', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(lh_group, 'C6', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.place_in_area(toolkit_group, 'D4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.7)
        
        toolkit_group.set_opacity(0)
        
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFD700"), FadeIn(sq_group), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00BFFF"), FadeIn(ed_group), run_time=1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF6347"), FadeIn(lh_group), run_time=1)
        
        # Final
        self.play(FadeIn(toolkit_group), run_time=1.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering Limits: From Intuition to L'Hôpital's Rule

sections.title: The Intuition of Limits: The Squirrel's Path
sections.content: Introduce the limit concept using a squirrel approaching a tree hollow. Even if the squirrel doesn't reach the exact point (x=c), it knows where it is heading. Use a graphical plot showing a curve with a hole at a specific point, illustrating that the limit is the 'destination' value (L).
sections.example: Visualize a squirrel moving along the curve y = (x²-1)/(x-1). As x approaches 1, the squirrel gets closer and closer to height 2, even though the point at x=1 is a 'hollow' (undefined).

sections.title: The Rigorous Foundation: Epsilon-Delta Definition
sections.content: Transition to the formal definition: 'For every epsilon > 0, there exists a delta > 0 such that if 0 < |x-c| < delta, then |f(x)-L| < epsilon.' Use an animation of a shrinking 'target box' (epsilon) around the limit and a corresponding 'input box' (delta) around c.
sections.example: Imagine a drone pilot trying to keep a delivery package within a tiny height-tolerance (epsilon). The definition guarantees that if the pilot stays within a horizontal range (delta) of the target, the package height remains within the tolerance.

sections.title: Indeterminate Forms & L'Hôpital's Rule
sections.content: Introduce the challenge of 0/0. Explain L'Hôpital's Rule as a tool to evaluate limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator separately when they both approach zero. Visual: Show two racing curves (f(x) and g(x)) both flattening to zero, and demonstrate how their ratio of slopes helps find the limit.
sections.example: Calculate lim(x→0) sin(x)/x. Visually represent sin(x) and x as two paths approaching the origin; show that the ratio of their tangent lines (cos(x)/1) equals 1 at x=0.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Limit Toolkit
sections.content: Summarize the flow: Epsilon-Delta provides the logical proof, while L'Hôpital's Rule provides the computational shortcut. Reiterate that limits bridge the gap between static algebra and dynamic calculus.
sections.example: A quick recap animation: The squirrel (Intuition) reaches the goal, the drone (Epsilon-Delta) verifies the safety, and the derivative (L'Hôpital) calculates the velocity to get there efficiently.
